newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka unit strike creates gas shortage.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka unit strike creates gas shortage.

text.p: A strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, is threatening the Indian Ocean island's gas supplies, newspapers said on Sunday.

The Island newspaper said thousands of consumers could run out of gas and many restaurants forced to close if the strike at Shell Gas Lanka Ltd, which began on Thursday, continues to disrupt supplies.
A company statement said it was making arrangements to supply gas to essential services like hospitals and the armed forces and urged employees to return to work.

The labour action came after Shell Gas Lanka suspended nine employees following a breach of safety regulations at Colombo port when gas was being unloaded, the firm's statement said, but did not give further details.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.

Shell Overseas Investment BV, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, bought a majority stake in the state-owned gas monopoly in October last year for $37 million under the government's programme to privatise state enterprises.

The company is currently embroiled in a dispute with the government after it increased the price of domestic gas twice in one year by more than 10 precent in total, in an apparent violation of the privatisation deal.

The Public Enterprises Reforms Commission, which handles privatisations, has said Shell was given a five-year gas distribution monopoly under the privatisation deal on the condition that prices could only be raised by 10 percent a year.
